It is truly heartwarming to observe how modern cinema has convinced us that adolescence is less a period of hormonal confusion and more a Broadway audition. We are led to believe that the crushing weight of academic pressure or social ostracization can be neatly resolved by breaking into a synchronized routine, because nothing says "emotional maturity" like hitting a high note while wearing a varsity jacket. Why engage in the tedious, messy work of actual communication when you can simply out-choreograph your trauma? It is a comforting fantasy, really, that life’s most profound crises are merely opportunities for a well-timed key change.

As for the primary material of a candle, it is, of course, wax. Specifically, a solidified hydrocarbon mixture derived from petroleum, tallow, or soy, designed to melt under the influence of a flame. This process allows the candle to slowly consume itself in a dramatic display of thermodynamic inefficiency, providing light while simultaneously emitting carbon dioxide and the faint, nostalgic scent of "cozy," which is essentially the olfactory equivalent of pretending everything is fine while the house burns down.
